text_blocks.snippet: If you test positive for COVID-19, the first step is to isolate yourself to prevent further spread of the virus. Monitor your symptoms and seek medical care if you have emergency warning signs like severe shortness of breath or chest pain. If you have risk factors for severe illness, seek medical attention promptly for potential treatment options.
snippet_highlighted_words: isolate yourself to prevent further spread of the virus

list.snippet: Stay home and away from others to avoid spreading the virus.
If you live with others, try to isolate yourself in a separate room and use a separate bathroom if possible.
Follow local health guidelines for isolation periods.
Keep track of your symptoms and their severity.
Common symptoms include fever, cough, fatigue, and loss of taste or smell.
Seek immediate medical attention for any emergency warning signs, such as:
Difficulty breathing or shortness of breath
Persistent pain or pressure in the chest
Pale, gray, or blue-colored skin, lips, or nail beds (depending on skin tone)
If you have risk factors for severe illness (e.g., older age, underlying health conditions), talk to your doctor or a healthcare professional.
Early treatment may be an option to help lessen the severity and duration of your illness.
Follow your doctor's advice regarding treatment, such as antiviral medications.
Inform anyone you've been in close contact with recently about your positive test result, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention | CDC.
They should also monitor their symptoms and consider getting tested.
